ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based pre-incorporation screening of every UBO (direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more), all directors, and authorized signatories against the following: FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) criteria under PCMLTFA s. 11.1 and S.O.R./2002-184; the consolidated United Nations Security Council sanctions lists via Global Affairs Canada; the Canadian sanctions regulations enacted under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List for all USD-denominated wire transfers and PayPal rails; and where relevant the United Kingdom and European Union consolidated lists. Screening is refreshed at least annually, upon any change of UBO or director, and before any significant transaction; nil-hit results must be documented with notarized and apostilled self-declarations for foreign UBOs; positive hits are escalated immediately to designated counsel and the transaction is blocked pending legal and regulatory clearance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction) utilizing the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system and online filings through authorized Alberta Corporate Registry service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta corporate names must contain a distinctive alphanumeric element, optional descriptive or connecting elements, and a mandatory legal element ('Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited', 'Corp.', 'Inc.', 'Ltd.' or French equivalents). Names in non-Latin scripts such as CJK, Cyrillic, Arabic, or Devanagari must be romanized into Latin characters in the NUANS submission; only the transliterated form is validated and reserved. The proposed name must not be confusingly similar to any existing Alberta or federal corporate name, trade-mark record, or registered trade name detected by NUANS, and must not falsely imply government affiliation, regulated professional status, or licensing authority that the corporation does not hold.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS-based name reservation is valid for 90 calendar days from issuance and may be renewed by paying the applicable extension tariff before expiry. If the Alberta Corporate Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant may, within 30 days of the rejection notice, file a written reconsideration request with Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction accompanied by a fresh NUANS report, the specific legal grounds distinguishing the proposed name from the cited conflicting names, and any supporting evidence of use or goodwill. If administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an application for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta or, more efficiently, re-file under a different distinctive element with a new NUANS report; registration fees are non-refundable upon rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical civic street address within the Province of Alberta is mandatory and may not be a post-office box. A virtual-office package comprising a real street address, mail scanning and forwarding, occupied premises during Alberta business hours, and custody of corporate records at that address is permissible and acceptable for this low-risk ISIC 7490 creative game-art outsourcing business, provided the provider holds the premises and accepts service of process in Alberta.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 8% annualized probability of an unannounced on-site inspection for a low-risk, standard-tier ISIC 7490 outsourcing corporation; the likelihood elevates to roughly 25% where the ISC/UBO register is deficient, corporate records are inaccessible, filings are delinquent, or a sanctions/PEP hit occurs. Inspections may be conducted by Corporate Registry compliance officers or, in AML/CFT matters, by FINTRAC or RCMP under warrant.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 — Sections 5 to 13 (incorporation), Section 27 (articles), Section 101 (registered office), Sections 106 to 120 (directors and officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Service Alberta — Corporate Registry (Registrar of Corporations), Alberta Corporate Registry, Edmonton, Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form INC-1) filed electronically through the Alberta Corporate Registry Web Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; incorporation may proceed with zero fully paid share capital, and no escrow account or capital deposit requirement applies. The board of directors may authorize the issuance of shares for such consideration as the board determines, including cash, property, or past services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Corporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) is accepted, and the Articles of Incorporation as certified are confirmed and ratified. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be fixed at [Registered Office Address], in the City of Calgary, Province of Alberta, and that [Firm Name] is appointed registered records agent under Section 101 of the Act. FURTHER RESOLVED, that subscriptions for 100 Class A Common Voting Shares are approved, deemed fully paid by cash and contributed services, and the initial directors are confirmed. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the following individuals are appointed officers: [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary-Treasurer, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the first annual general meeting of shareholders.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta — Corporate Registry (via authorized service provider or Alberta Corporate Registry Web Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Corporate Name Search Request (NUANS name search report) for proposed name 'AAA GAME ART OUTSOURCING INC.' or a numbered company option. Review the preliminary name search results, confirm availability, and reserve the approved name for 90 days through the registry portal. If restricted or objectionable words are contained, file supporting consents or select a distinct alternative.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name request form
Proposed corporate name and up to three alternatives
Statutory declaration of entitlement to use the name
Consent letters from individuals or entities if name includes restricted words
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused on grounds of conflict or distinctiveness, submit alternative names within the 90-day reservation window. A conditional approval may be requested where only minor textual distinction exists, and the reservation period may be renewed upon registry discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation (Form INC-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Service Alberta online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file Form INC-1 electronically through the Alberta Corporate Registry online system. Attach the NUANS name search report reference, declare the registered office street address in Alberta (post office boxes are not permissible), list the initial directors (minimum one, majority must be Canadian residents), and define the authorized share structure including Class A Common Voting Shares and Class B Preferred Shares. Pay the statutory fee of CAD 250 by credit card via the portal and retain the electronic acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Form INC-1 executed by each incorporator
NUANS name search report reference and reservation number
Registered office address and registered records agent consent
Initial directors consent and residency declaration
Shareholder agreement draft and share class memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or rejection notice, refile the corrected Article text and Form INC-1 through the same portal within the outstanding reservation period. Registry fees are credited or waived where rejection is attributable to administrative error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation and the certified Articles of Incorporation from the portal. Establish the corporate minute book, prepare board and shareholder records, issue share certificates consistent with the approved board resolution, and affix the corporate seal if adopted by the board.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued electronically)
Certified text of Articles of Incorporation
Corporate minute book and share certificate ledger
Registered records agent consent letter
Shareholder register and director/officer register forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a certificate is lost or defective, request a duplicate certificate through the registry upon payment of the requisite service fee. Any textual error in the Articles shall be corrected by filing Articles of Amendment under Section 27 of the Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting and Initial Officer Installation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (registered office or remote written consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first organizational board meeting, or circulate a unanimous written resolution in lieu of meeting, and adopt Bylaw No. 1 governing corporate affairs. Ratify the incorporation expenses, confirm the pro-forma board resolution, elect the initial directors, appoint the President, Secretary-Treasurer and Chief Financial Officer, approve the corporate bank account authorizations, and adopt the corporate seal and signature policy.
required_dossiers: Executed pro-forma first board resolution
Bylaw No. 1 (adopted by the board)
Organization meeting minutes or unanimous written consent
Officer appointment and acceptance forms
Bank account signature cards and AML/KYC pack for financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If quorum is not attained, reconvene the meeting upon two clear days' written notice to all directors. Any procedural defect in the meeting may be cured by a subsequent unanimous written consent of all directors pursuant to subsection 114(8) of the Alberta Business Corporations Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number Registration and Municipal Business Licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online (BRO); City of Calgary Licensing and Business Services; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance — Corporate Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA within 30 days of incorporation through Business Registration Online to obtain a nine-digit Business Number. Enrol for the Corporation Tax program (RC0001), the GST/HST program (RC0002) electively where annual taxable supply exceeds CAD 30,000, and the Alberta Corporate Income Tax program. Concurrently apply for a municipal general business licence for the Calgary registered office, ensuring the zoning bylaw permits office-based creative and digital production services under NAICS 541430.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Registered office address proof (lease agreement or ownership deed)
Board resolution designating the premises as head office and principal place of business
Directors and officers identification documentation
Business activity declaration referencing ISIC 7490 and NAICS 541430
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA enrolment is incomplete or rejected, correct the application and resubmit through the BRO portal with amendment notices. Municipal licence denials based on zoning may be appealed to the Calgary Subdivision and Development Appeal Board under the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c M-26.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade — Investment Alberta (sectoral industrial licensing not applicable to digital art outsourcing; no provincial sector-specific permit is triggered)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — municipal General Business Licence (Class A office occupancy) is the only operational permit required for the Calgary-based 3D art production studio

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA), Alberta Government
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category A (purely office/studio use, no EIA registration or environmental assessment order required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-3, Schedule 1)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams are generated by the 3D modeling and rigging studio; compliance is limited to municipal solid waste diversion bylaws, indoor air quality and ventilation performance under the Alberta Building Code, and regulated disposal of spent electronic media and IT hardware through authorized e-waste recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code for low-hazard office occupancy, including annual fire inspection by the municipal fire authority, presence of portable extinguishers, illuminated exit signage, and emergency evacuation plans. Structural load clearance for server and render-farm floor loading certified by a professional engineer where raised flooring or concentrated equipment is installed, in accordance with Alberta Building Code Part 4. Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) clearance through Alberta Workplace Health and Safety under the OHS Act, requiring completion of a workplace hazard assessment, WHMIS training where applicable, and implementation of ergonomic and emergency-response policies for creative production staff.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement. There are no exchange control regulations, no capital account restrictions, and no central bank approval is required for current account or capital account transactions. Dividends, royalties, service fees, and return of capital may be freely remitted overseas, subject only to applicable Canadian withholding taxes and the account provider's standard AML/KYC verification. Non-resident ownership of an Alberta business corporation is permitted; the Investment Canada Act requires only statutory notification or pre-merger review for acquisitions of control above specified thresholds and does not impede ordinary treasury flows. Practical hurdles are limited to enhanced due diligence, sanctions screening, and tax-residency declarations required by Canadian banks and FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export proceeds surrender rules in Canada. Exporters and service providers may invoice, collect, and retain export proceeds in any freely usable currency without any statutory timeline for conversion or repatriation to Canada. Conversion of foreign receipts into CAD is optional and is executed at market rates agreed with the commercial bank; no mandatory conversion ratio or surrender mechanism applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — offshore EMI licences (e.g., UK FCA or EEA EMI) are not recognized by OSFI as deposit-taking institutions and cannot open Canadian-dollar settlement accounts in the Canadian banking system. Such entities may be able to provide cross-border payments only through a licensed Canadian payment processor, and any entity that engages in money services business in Canada is required to register with FINTRAC as a money services business and comply with AML/sanctions screening. For a corporate treasury that requires stable CAD liquidity, enforceable bank guarantees, and tax documentation, a Schedule I chartered bank account is mandatory; EMIs can be used only as an auxiliary payment rail after primary bank onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for Alberta-incorporated companies with local directors, using bank-approved video identity verification and digital signatures under FINTRAC's Client Due Diligence rules. When any director or beneficial owner is a non-resident, or when the corporation lacks an established trading history, the bank may require an in-person or live video compliance interview with at least one director before final approval. Notarized corporate resolutions, a current certificate of incumbency, valid government-issued identification for all directors and significant shareholders, and a physical registered-office address in Alberta are accepted as the standard documentation package.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners or a multi-layered offshore parent holding 25% or more of the corporation's equity without transparent corporate substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extract for the Alberta company; register of directors and shareholders; a clear organizational chart with ultimate beneficial owners; a notarized corporate authorization naming signatories; legal authorization from the foreign parent; business licence or game-art portfolio evidence establishing substance; proof of physical office lease or employment contracts; and a beneficial-ownership declaration executed under oath.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial deposit is sourced from a high-value wire from a foreign parent or client without a stated commercial purpose or source-of-wealth narrative.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed board resolution authorizing the account transfer; the inward remittance instruction marked 'INWARD EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' or 'TRADE PREPAYMENT'; a signed master service agreement or share subscription agreement; the corresponding invoice or capital contribution statement; the originator's bank account statement; and a detailed source-of-funds declaration supported by corporate financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate activity description is vague or suggests prohibited or higher-risk sectors such as gambling, cryptocurrency, NFTs, or unhandled virtual asset payments within the game-art value chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed project contracts with named AAA game studios; a production pipeline description confirming exclusively 3D sculpting, rigging, and art asset delivery; NAICS/ISIC code mapping to 541430/7490; a contractual exclusion of crypto-gambling and NFT services; and a written compliance attestation that no payments are made from or to sanctioned jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected revenue stream is inconsistent with the low-risk profile of a creative BPO company, or treasury flows involve rapid pass-through payments via third parties with no demonstrated commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year business and cash-flow plan; a complete client list with jurisdiction and onboarding details; supplier or subcontractor agreements evidencing the need for pass-through payments; payroll and corporate tax remittance records; and periodic FINTRAC/OSFI-compliant internal AML risk assessments and audit trail documentation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity investment from a foreign parent should be routed via SWIFT MT103 (or equivalent cross-border wire) to the corporation's CAD operating account at a Schedule I Canadian bank. The remittance advice must contain a clear purpose text such as 'INWARD EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' and, where available, an ISO 20022 purpose code of 'EQUI' or 'GDDS' for investment-related transfers. Although Canada does not mandate a specific purpose code, the bank's AML system requires consistency between the beneficiary name, the corporate registry number, the amount, and the supporting board resolution. For non-resident investment above Investment Canada Act thresholds, attach the corresponding notice/advisory reference to the file. There is no central bank exchange-control approval; however, any single wire of CAD 10,000 or more triggers ordinary reporting and may require the originator's bank to verify the underlying transaction documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements to foreign subcontractors and vendors should be executed using SWIFT MT103 for standard settlement when the amount is below the required documentary control threshold, and through an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) opened at the Canadian bank where milestone payments exceed the bank's defined risk threshold or where the beneficiary requires payment security. For CAD-denominated domestic settlements, use Canada's Lynx high-value payment system or standard EFT/Interac-commercial grade rails. For USD-denominated disbursements within Canada or cross-border, use US-dollar clearing through the bank's US correspondent network or the Canadian Automated Clearing Settlement System. Each outbound payment should be accompanied by the underlying invoice, purchase order, delivery confirmation, and a payment-purpose narrative referencing the applicable milestone or contract clause to avoid OFAC, FINTRAC, or OSFI alert delays.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (FXA) for CAD/USD and other G10 currencies under an ISDA Master Agreement or standardized Canadian bank foreign-exchange forward contract.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to local conversion restrictions (e.g., KRW, CNY offshore variants) when hedging subsidiary receipts; NDFs are not applicable to CAD itself, as CAD is fully deliverable.
FX swaps for short-term liquidity flows where the corporation holds intercompany netting in multiple currencies and needs to avoid end-of-day daylight overdrafts.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-duration matching of USD-denominated client contracts against CAD-denominated operating costs, including doquiver-in-advance settlement provisions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta annual return for an Alberta-incorporated corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, through an authorized Alberta registry agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File each year within two months after the corporation's anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing can lead to administrative dissolution after the statutory notice and process; there is no universal fixed strike-off date. Registry-agent service fees are additional.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal annual return, if the corporation is federally incorporated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years can result in dissolution under the Canada Business Corporations Act, subject to statutory notice and process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta corporate income tax return (AT1), if the corporation has an Alberta filing obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, acting for Alberta corporate income tax administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due six months after the corporation's taxation year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and arrears interest may apply; the filing obligation and penalties depend on the corporation's tax circumstances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due six months after the corporation's taxation year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and arrears interest may apply; repeated or prolonged non-compliance can lead to collection and enforcement action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Alberta corporation generally requires an auditor unless shareholders pass the permitted unanimous resolution dispensing with an auditor for the financial year. A distributing corporation cannot use this exemption. A federally incorporated corporation may dispense with an auditor only by the applicable unanimous shareholder resolution and if it is not a distributing corporation. No general revenue or asset threshold alone triggers the exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) are generally available to qualifying private enterprises. Tax returns use Canadian income tax rules and may require tax-to-book reconciliations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An Alberta corporation must maintain an individuals-with-significant-control register, take reasonable steps to keep it accurate, and update it at least once during each financial year and within 15 days after becoming aware of a relevant change. Record share transfers and reassess control; the Alberta register is not routinely filed with the annual return. Federal corporations must update their individuals-with-significant-control register at least annually and file required information with Corporations Canada.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book, including required resolutions and meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100-500 annually; Alberta registered-office and agent requirements apply, and registry-agent service charges may be additional.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000-10,000 for a small private corporation; scope, transaction volume, and reporting complexity materially affect fees.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined on general business income (federal 15% + Alberta 8%); 11% combined active business rate for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligible for the federal small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income (federal 9% + Alberta 2%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday is available to creative BPO studios in Canada or Alberta. Applicable structural incentives include the CCPC small business deduction, SR&ED investment tax credits (35% refundable for CCPCs, otherwise 15% non-refundable) for qualifying R&D, and normal deduction timing for direct labour, software, and overhead. Routine game-art outsourcing and character rigging are unlikely to qualify for SR&ED; claims require rigorous technical documentation. Alberta imposes no separate provincial investment credit for this industry.
